title: Synology patches critical DSM OAuth flaw (CVSS 9.8) and NGINX HTTP/2 flaw (CVSS 8.1)
date_note: Date the Synology advisories SA_26_21 and SA_26_20 were published.
summary: Synology published two advisories on 19 November. CVE-2026-120382 (CVSS 9.8) lets a remote attacker without an account read or write arbitrary files or cause denial of service through the DSM OAuth API. CVE-2026-123007 (CVSS 8.1) is an NGINX HTTP/2 heap overflow. Fixes for DSM 7.3 and 7.4 are due by 20 November; the advisories do not mention exploitation.
plain: Synology has warned of two serious flaws in the software of its NAS storage devices. Fixed versions are due by 20 November; until then the vendor gives workarounds.
exec: NAS devices often hold backups and shared files; an unauthenticated flaw in them is a data-loss and ransomware risk if exposed to the internet.
action: Install DSM 7.4.1-90080-2 or 7.3.2-86009-6 when released; meanwhile deactivate the OAuth Service package and disable HTTP/2 in Control Panel, and keep NAS devices off the internet.
impact: DSM 7.1 to 7.4 and BeeStation OS 1.5 are listed as affected; DSM 7.2.x, 7.1 and BeeStation OS had no fix yet when read (advisories marked Ongoing).

validation.note: Vendor advisories read in full; GBHackers independently reports the same CVEs and scores. No exploitation stated by either.

review.note: SA_26_21 and SA_26_20 (Nov 19): CVEs, CVSS 9.8 and 8.1, fix builds, scheduled by 2026-11-20 wording in SA_26_21, workarounds, no exploitation; GBHackers matches
